accepted.question: Describe the Chinese Wall security model, including its two rules, and state the specific concern it addresses.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall simple security rule permits access to an object only if it is in the same company dataset as objects already accessed by the subject, or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: A subject s can be granted access to an object o only if the object: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s, that is, "within the Wall," or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall *-property permits write access only if access is permitted by the simple security rule and no object can be read that is in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested and contains unsanitized information.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall model is designed to address conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash's Chinese Wall Policy is designed to address a very specific concern: conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall is an access control confidentiality policy, not an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy is sensitive to the history of past accesses, so permissions change dynamically.
marking_points.quote: The Chinese Wall is an access control policy in which accesses are sensitive to the history of past accesses.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy is a hybrid model proposed by Brewer and Nash in 1989.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash (1989) proposed a policy called the Chinese Wall Policy that addresses such conflicts of interest.

marking_points.quote: access control matrix (ACM) Capabilities (C-List) access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.point: An access control list is an object-centered description of access rights.

marking_points.point: The access control matrix is a basic control structure.

marking_points.point: An advantage of the access control matrix is clarity of definition.

marking_points.point: A disadvantage of the access control matrix is poor scalability.

questions.question: Discuss six distinct malware attack techniques or propagation methods described in the lecture material, explaining how each operates or spreads.

marking_points.point: A virus can propagate by appending a virus body to an existing program and altering the program header to switch the entry point to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus Jump to the original entry point during execution

marking_points.point: A rootkit masks malicious processes and software to ensure privileged remote access, often installed after a vulnerability is found.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware steals user logins and passwords, logs keystrokes, and can redirect browsers to unwanted sites.
marking_points.quote: They steal user logins and passwords, document sites visited, log keystrokes and even redirect browsers to unwanted sites.

marking_points.point: The Morris worm propagated by using a debugging feature of sendmail for remote execution.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution) Propagated in the Arpanet

marking_points.point: Elk Cloner spread via boot sector infection and hooked the reset handler to execute its payload.
marking_points.quote: A program spread via boot sector infection On every 50-th reset a short poem was is played by hooking the reset handler

marking_points.point: XSS attacks inject malicious JavaScript into a user's browser, which can execute arbitrary code.
marking_points.quote: Allows execution of arbitrary Javascript in user’s browser.

questions.question: Describe the Chinese Wall security model, including its two rules, and state the specific concern it addresses.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall simple security rule permits access to an object only if it is in the same company dataset as objects already accessed by the subject, or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: A subject s can be granted access to an object o only if the object: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s, that is, “within the Wall,” or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall *-property permits write access only if access is permitted by the simple security rule and no object can be read that is in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested and contains unsanitized information.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall model is designed to address conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash’s Chinese Wall Policy is designed to address a very specific concern: conflicts of interest by a consultant or contractor.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall is an access control confidentiality policy, not an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy is sensitive to the history of past accesses, so permissions change dynamically.
marking_points.quote: The Chinese Wall is an access control policy in which accesses are sensitive to the history of past accesses.

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall policy is a hybrid model proposed by Brewer and Nash in 1989.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash (1989) proposed a policy called the Chinese Wall Policy that addresses such conflicts of interest.

questions.question: State four distinct steps in the Samy worm's propagation and impact, as described in the lecture material.

marking_points.point: The worm injects JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It obtains the list of a user's heroes via a GET request on a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It adds Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile gets their profile infected and their friends list infected with Samy.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: Eventually about one million MySpace profiles were infected.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The attack exploits the fact that JavaScript is dynamically injected from a third-party, a cross-site.
marking_points.quote: In a XSS attack, Javascript does not originate from a web server but is dynamically injected into it via a user request a following reﬂection from a third-party, a “cross-site”.

questions.question: Describe six preventive network security mechanisms that can be deployed to protect an organization's network, and for each mechanism explain its primary function.

marking_points.point: Firewall controls incoming and outgoing traffic based on security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Proxy server improves data security and network performance by acting as a firewall and web filter, and caching data.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation creates boundaries between network segments based on common function, risk, or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: Remote Access VPN provides secure remote access to the organization network for individual hosts or clients.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) ensures a user only has access and permissions required to fulfill their role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) detect or prevent network security attacks such as brute force, DoS, and exploits.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.
